002
003import java.io.IOException;
004import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
005import java.net.URI;
006import java.nio.ByteBuffer;
007import java.nio.CharBuffer;
008import java.nio.charset.CharacterCodingException;
009import java.nio.charset.Charset;
010import java.nio.charset.CharsetEncoder;
011import java.nio.charset.CodingErrorAction;
012import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
013import java.util.Objects;
014
015import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
016
017import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogOutput.ContentType;
018import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogOutput.ContentType.StandardContentType;
019import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogOutput.WriteMethod;
020import io.jstach.rainbowgum.format.AbstractStandardEventFormatter;
021import io.jstach.rainbowgum.format.StandardEventFormatter;
022
023/**
024 * Encodes a {@link LogEvent} into a buffer of its choosing. While the {@link Buffer} does
025 * not need to be thread-safe the encoder itself should be.
026 * <p>
027 * An appender typically calls an encoder by first {@linkplain #buffer(BufferHints)
028 * creating a buffer} that the encoder knows about or reusing an existing {@link Buffer}
029 * the encoder knows about.
030 * <p>
031 * The {@linkplain #encode(LogEvent, Buffer) encoding into a buffer} typically happens
032 * outside of lock to minimize lock contention. Thus the appender promises not to share a
033 * buffer at the same time with other threads as well as only use a buffer the log encoder
034 * created at some point.
035 * <p>
036 * Once encoding is done the appender than typically enters into a lock (appenders
037 * attached to an async publisher may not need to use a lock) where the appender will ask
038 * the buffer to {@linkplain Buffer#drain(LogOutput, LogEvent) drain} its contents into
039 * the output.
040 * <p>
041 * Because {@link Buffer} is not a specific implementation the Encoder typically casts the
042 * buffer to the expected concrete implementation. {@link AbstractEncoder} can make this
043 * logic easier and is recommended to extend it.
044 * <p>
045 * Given the complexity of encoders it is recommend use the much easier to implement
046 * interface of {@link LogFormatter} and convert it to an encoder with
047 * {@link #of(LogFormatter)}.
048 *
049 * @see LogFormatter
050 * @see Buffer
051 * @see LogAppender
052 */
053public interface LogEncoder {
054
055        /**
056         * Creates a <strong>new</strong> buffer. The encoder should not try to reuse buffers
057         * as that is the responsibility of the {@linkplain LogAppender appender} (and
058         * possibly {@link LogOutput} but usually not). Hints can be retrieved by call
059         * {@link LogOutput#bufferHints()}.
060         * @param hints hints are like size and storage type etc.
061         * @return a new buffer.
062         * @apiNote hints can be retrieved by calling {@link LogOutput#bufferHints()} the
063         * reason the output itself is not passed is to prevent the buffer from using the
064         * output directly at an inappropriate time as well as the rare possibility of the
065         * buffer being used by multiple outputs.
066         */
067        public Buffer buffer(BufferHints hints);
068
069        /**
070         * Encodes an event to the buffer. It is recommended that the encoder call
071         * {@link Buffer#clear()} before using.
072         * @param event log event.
073         * @param buffer buffer created from {@link #buffer(BufferHints)}.
074         */
075        public void encode(LogEvent event, Buffer buffer);
076
077        /**
078         * Creates an encoder from a formatter that encodes with
079         * {@link StandardCharsets#UTF_8}. For anything more than the default charset/content
080         * type/max buffer size use {@link #builder(LogFormatter)}.
081         * @param formatter formatter.
082         * @return encoder.
083         */
084        public static LogProvider<LogEncoder> of(LogFormatter formatter) {
085                return builder(formatter).build();
086        }
087
088        /**
089         * Creates a builder for an encoder backed by the given formatter.
090         * @param formatter formatter.
091         * @return builder.
092         */
093        public static Builder builder(LogFormatter formatter) {
094                return new Builder(formatter);
095        }
096
097        /**
098         * Creates a builder for an encoder backed by the default TTLL
099         * ({@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.format.StandardEventFormatter}) formatter.
100         * @return builder.
101         */
102        public static Builder builder() {
103                return new Builder(StandardEventFormatter.builder().build());
104        }
105
106        /**
107         * Builds a {@link LogEncoder} out of a {@link LogFormatter}.
108         *
109         * @apiNote created with {@link LogEncoder#builder(LogFormatter)} or
110         * {@link LogEncoder#builder()}.
111         */
112        public static final class Builder {
113
114                private final LogFormatter formatter;
115
116                private @Nullable Charset charset;
117
118                private @Nullable ContentType contentType;
119
120                private int maxBufferSize = -1;
121
122                private int initialBufferSize = DirectByteBufferBuffer.DEFAULT_INITIAL_BYTE_CAPACITY;
123
124                private @Nullable Boolean useGetBytes;
125
126                private @Nullable String description;
127
128                private Builder(LogFormatter formatter) {
129                        this.formatter = Objects.requireNonNull(formatter);
130                }
131
132                /**
133                 * A human readable description of the formatter/pattern this encoder was built
134                 * from (e.g. the actual pattern string), surfaced by
135                 * {@link LogReporter.Reportable} instead of the built encoder only ever showing
136                 * up as its bare concrete class name. Purely diagnostic: has no effect on
137                 * encoding itself.
138                 * @param description description, or <code>null</code> for none.
139                 * @return this.
140                 */
141                public Builder description(@Nullable String description) {
142                        this.description = description;
143                        return this;
144                }
145
146                /**
147                 * Charset to encode with. Only affects outputs whose
148                 * {@link BufferHints#writeMethod()} is {@link WriteMethod#BYTES} or
149                 * {@link WriteMethod#BYTE_BUFFER} - the {@link WriteMethod#STRING} path hands a
150                 * plain {@link String} to {@link LogOutput#write(LogEvent, String)}, whose own
151                 * default implementation is fixed to {@link StandardCharsets#UTF_8} regardless of
152                 * this setting, but no built-in output actually uses that write method. Defaults
153                 * to {@link StandardCharsets#UTF_8}, or to {@link #contentType(ContentType)}'s
154                 * own charset if that was set and this was not. If both are set this charset is
155                 * what is actually used to encode; {@link #contentType(ContentType)} still
156                 * controls what is reported to the output.
157                 * @param charset charset to encode with.
158                 * @return this.
159                 */
160                public Builder charset(Charset charset) {
161                        this.charset = Objects.requireNonNull(charset);
162                        return this;
163                }
164
165                /**
166                 * Content type reported to the output. Use this when the formatter produces
167                 * something other than plain text. Defaults to
168                 * {@link StandardContentType#TEXT_PLAIN} with whatever charset is in effect (see
169                 * {@link #charset(Charset)}).
170                 * @param contentType content type reported to the output.
171                 * @return this.
172                 */
173                public Builder contentType(ContentType contentType) {
174                        this.contentType = Objects.requireNonNull(contentType);
175                        return this;
176                }
177
178                /**
179                 * Configures a maximum buffer size - see {@link Buffer#isOversized()}. This is a
180                 * <strong>soft ceiling, not a hard cap</strong>: a single event can still grow
181                 * the buffer past this size while it is being encoded (nothing here truncates or
182                 * rejects an oversized event), it just means the buffer's backing storage gets
183                 * shrunk back down afterward instead of being kept at its grown size indefinitely
184                 * - a quota that gets reclaimed after the fact, not enforced during the write.
185                 * This, like charset, is a property of the encoder/buffer itself, not of whatever
186                 * ends up reusing the buffer (e.g. an appender's {@code ThreadLocal}-cached one)
187                 * - the buffer decides for itself, inside its own {@link Buffer#clear()}, whether
188                 * to shrink.
189                 * @param maxBufferSize a negative value disables {@link Buffer#isOversized()}
190                 * entirely (the default).
191                 * @return this.
192                 */
193                public Builder maxBufferSize(int maxBufferSize) {
194                        this.maxBufferSize = maxBufferSize;
195                        return this;
196                }
197
198                /**
199                 * The capacity a fresh buffer is allocated with before any event has been encoded
200                 * into it. Defaults to
201                 * {@link DirectByteBufferBuffer#DEFAULT_INITIAL_BYTE_CAPACITY}.
202                 * @param initialBufferSize initial buffer capacity, must be positive.
203                 * @return this.
204                 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if not positive.
205                 */
206                public Builder initialBufferSize(int initialBufferSize) {
207                        if (initialBufferSize <= 0) {
208                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("initialBufferSize must be positive: " + initialBufferSize);
209                        }
210                        this.initialBufferSize = initialBufferSize;
211                        return this;
212                }
213
214                /**
215                 * If set, converts to bytes with {@link String#getBytes(Charset)} on the fully
216                 * formatted string instead of the default
217                 * {@link java.nio.charset.CharsetEncoder}-based copy directly into a reused byte
218                 * buffer. Only affects {@link WriteMethod#BYTES}/{@link WriteMethod#BYTE_BUFFER}
219                 * outputs - always calls the byte[] overload directly regardless of which of
220                 * those two hints an output actually declares.
221                 * <p>
222                 * If never called, this resolves to {@code true} instead of the historical
223                 * {@code false} default when {@link LogProperties#GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY} is
224                 * enabled and the process is running as a GraalVM native image - see that
225                 * property's javadoc for what it currently resolves to and why that is not a
226                 * contract. Calling this method, either way, always wins over that.
227                 * @param useGetBytes default is false, unless left unset and overridden by
228                 * {@link LogProperties#GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY}.
229                 * @return this.
230                 */
231                public Builder useGetBytes(boolean useGetBytes) {
232                        this.useGetBytes = useGetBytes;
233                        return this;
234                }
235
236                /**
237                 * Builds the encoder.
238                 * @return encoder.
239                 */
240                public LogProvider<LogEncoder> build() {
241                        Charset c = charset;
242                        ContentType ct = contentType;
243                        if (ct != null) {
244                                if (c == null) {
245                                        c = ct.charsetOrNull();
246                                }
247                        }
248                        if (c == null) {
249                                c = StandardCharsets.UTF_8;
250                        }
251                        if (ct == null) {
252                                ct = ContentType.of(StandardContentType.TEXT_PLAIN.contentType(), c);
253                        }
254                        var resolvedCharset = c;
255                        var resolvedContentType = ct;
256                        Boolean explicitUseGetBytes = useGetBytes;
257                        String resolvedDescription = description;
258                        return (n, config) -> {
259                                /*
260                                 * Resolved lazily, inside this lambda, not eagerly above: the global
261                                 * optimize flag is only guaranteed set by the time a real LogConfig
262                                 * exists (see DefaultLogConfig's constructor), which this lambda's config
263                                 * parameter proves has already happened - resolving it eagerly in build()
264                                 * could run before any LogConfig was ever constructed.
265                                 */
266                                boolean resolvedUseGetBytes = explicitUseGetBytes != null ? explicitUseGetBytes
267                                                : AbstractLogAppender.globalOptimizeEnabled && AbstractLogAppender.isNativeImageRuntime();
268                                return new FormatterEncoder(formatter, resolvedCharset, resolvedContentType, maxBufferSize,
269                                                initialBufferSize, resolvedUseGetBytes, config.metrics(), resolvedDescription);
270                        };
271                }
272
273        }
274
275        /**
276         * Provides a lazy loaded encoder from a URI.
277         * @param uri uri.
278         * @return provider of encoder.
279         */
280        public static LogProvider<LogEncoder> of(URI uri) {
281                return of(LogProviderRef.of(uri));
282        }
283
284        /**
285         * Provides the standard TTLL encoder.
286         * @return provider of encoder.
287         */
288        public static LogProvider<LogEncoder> ofTTLL() {
289                return of(LogProviderRef.of(URI.create(AbstractStandardEventFormatter.SCHEMA)));
290        }
291
292        /**
293         * Provides a lazy loaded encoder from a provider ref.
294         * @param ref uri.
295         * @return provider of output.
296         * @apiNote the provider may throw an {@link UncheckedIOException}.
297         */
298        public static LogProvider<LogEncoder> of(LogProviderRef ref) {
299                return (s, c) -> {
300                        return c.encoderRegistry().provide(ref).provide(s, c);
301                };
302        }
303
304        /**
305         * Finds output based on URI.
306         */
307        public interface EncoderProvider {
308
309                /**
310                 * Loads an encoder from a URI.
311                 * @param ref reference to provider usually just a uri.
312                 * @return output.
313                 * @throws LogProviderRef.NotFoundException if there is no registered provider.
314                 */
315                LogProvider<LogEncoder> provide(LogProviderRef ref) throws LogProviderRef.NotFoundException;
316
317                /**
318                 * Convenience method to register encoders that require no configuration.
319                 * @param encoder already configured encoder.
320                 * @return encoder provider.
321                 */
322                static EncoderProvider of(LogProvider<LogEncoder> encoder) {
323                        return ref -> encoder;
324                }
325
326        }
327
328        /**
329         * Encoders buffer.
330         */
331        public interface Buffer extends AutoCloseable {
332
333                /**
334                 * The appender will call this usually within a lock to transfer content from the
335                 * buffer to the output.
336                 * @param output output to receive content.
337                 * @param event log event.
338                 */
339                public void drain(LogOutput output, LogEvent event);
340
341                /**
342                 * Prepare the buffer for reuse.
343                 * <p>
344                 * An appender may not call clear before being passed to the encoder so the
345                 * encoder should do its own clearing.
346                 * <p>
347                 * Built-in implementations also shrink their own backing storage back down here
348                 * if {@link #isOversized()} - see that method - so a single unusually large event
349                 * does not permanently bloat a buffer that gets reused for many more events after
350                 * it.
351                 */
352                public void clear();
353
354                /**
355                 * Whether this buffer has grown large enough (its capacity, not how much of that
356                 * capacity the last event actually used) that its backing storage is worth
357                 * shrinking back down rather than kept at its grown size indefinitely - reused
358                 * buffers only grow on their own, they never shrink back down without deliberate
359                 * help. This is a soft ceiling checked between events, not a hard cap enforced
360                 * during one: nothing here stops a single event from growing the buffer past
361                 * whatever threshold it was configured with while that event is being encoded.
362                 * Built-in implementations consult this themselves inside {@link #clear()} to
363                 * decide whether to shrink their own backing storage in place (e.g.
364                 * {@link StringBuilder#trimToSize()}, or reallocating a smaller
365                 * {@link java.nio.ByteBuffer}) - most callers do not need to call this directly;
366                 * it remains here mainly for tests/observability and for a custom {@link Buffer}
367                 * implementation that wants the same self-shrinking behavior.
368                 * <p>
369                 * What "large enough" means, and whether it means anything at all, is entirely up
370                 * to the buffer/encoder - the same way charset is an encoder concern rather than
371                 * something an appender configures (see
372                 * {@link LogEncoder#builder(LogFormatter)}). The default implementation returns
373                 * {@code false} - a buffer implementation that does not override this, or an
374                 * encoder that never configured a threshold, never shrinks.
375                 * @return {@code true} if this buffer's backing storage has grown past whatever
376                 * threshold it was configured with.
377                 */
378                default boolean isOversized() {
379                        return false;
380                }
381
382                /**
383                 * Convenience that will call clear.
384                 */
385                @Override
386                default void close() {
387                        clear();
388                }
389
390        }
391
392        /**
393         * Hints the output can pass to the encoder for creating buffers like max size and
394         * storage style of the buffer etc.
395         *
396         * @apiNote There is no guarantees the encoder/buffer will honor these hints.
397         */
398        public interface BufferHints {
399
400                /*
401                 * TODO should we seal this?
402                 */
403
404                /**
405                 * The preferred write style of the output.
406                 * @return write method.
407                 * @apiNote {@link WriteMethod} implements this interface for convenience.
408                 */
409                LogOutput.WriteMethod writeMethod();
410
411                /**
412                 * Maximum size of the buffer. This is a way for the encoder to say it can only
413                 * handle so much data per event.
414                 * @return a negative number indicates size is not important.
415                 */
416                default int maximumSize() {
417                        return -1;
418                }
419
420        }
421
422        /**
423         * Abstract encoder that will cast the buffer to the desired implementation. Extend to
424         * make creating encoders easier.
425         *
426         * @param <T> buffer type.
427         */
428        abstract class AbstractEncoder<T extends Buffer> implements LogEncoder {
429
430                /**
431                 * Do nothing constructor.
432                 */
433                protected AbstractEncoder() {
434
435                }
436
437                /**
438                 * Create a specific buffer implementation.
439                 * @param hints buffer creation hints.
440                 * @return buffer
441                 */
442                protected abstract T doBuffer(BufferHints hints);
443
444                /**
445                 * A type safe version of {@link #encode(LogEvent, Buffer)}.
446                 * @param event event.
447                 * @param buffer casted buffer.
448                 */
449                protected abstract void doEncode(LogEvent event, T buffer);
450
451                @Override
452                public final Buffer buffer(BufferHints hints) {
453                        return doBuffer(hints);
454                }
455
456                @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
457                @Override
458                public final void encode(LogEvent event, Buffer buffer) {
459                        doEncode(event, (T) buffer);
460
461                }
462
463        }
464
465}
466
467/**
468 * A {@link LogEncoder.Buffer} that formats a {@link LogEvent} through a
469 * {@link LogFormatter} into some intermediate text representation before
470 * {@linkplain #drain(LogOutput, LogEvent) draining} it to the output - the common shape
471 * shared by {@link StringBuilderBuffer} and {@link DirectByteBufferBuffer}, letting
472 * {@link FormatterEncoder} dispatch to either without needing to know which concrete
473 * implementation it has.
474 */
475sealed interface TextBuffer extends LogEncoder.Buffer {
476
477        /**
478         * Formats {@code event} with {@code formatter} into this buffer's own backing
479         * storage, ready to be {@linkplain #drain(LogOutput, LogEvent) drained}. Does not
480         * call {@link #clear()} first - the caller is expected to do that.
481         * @param formatter formatter to format with.
482         * @param event event to format.
483         */
484        public void encodeToBuffer(LogFormatter formatter, LogEvent event);
485
486}
487
488/**
489 * A buffer that simply wraps a {@link StringBuilder}. Direct access to the
490 * {@link StringBuilder} is available as the field {@link #stringBuilder}.
491 *
492 * @see AbstractEncoder
493 */
494final class StringBuilderBuffer implements TextBuffer {
495
496        /**
497         * Underlying StringBuilder.
498         */
499        public final StringBuilder stringBuilder;
500
501        private final int maxBufferSize;
502
503        private final LogMetrics metrics;
504
505        /**
506         * Creates a StringBuilder based buffer that reports {@link #isOversized()} once
507         * {@code sb}'s capacity exceeds {@code maxBufferSize}, reporting
508         * {@link LogMetrics#BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC} to {@code metrics} each time
509         * {@link #clear()} actually shrinks the backing storage.
510         * @param sb string builder.
511         * @param maxBufferSize a negative value disables {@link #isOversized()} entirely
512         * (always {@code false}).
513         * @param metrics where to report {@link LogMetrics#BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC}.
514         * @return buffer.
515         */
516        public static StringBuilderBuffer of(StringBuilder sb, int maxBufferSize, LogMetrics metrics) {
517                return new StringBuilderBuffer(sb, maxBufferSize, metrics);
518        }
519
520        private StringBuilderBuffer(StringBuilder stringBuilder, int maxBufferSize, LogMetrics metrics) {
521                super();
522                this.stringBuilder = stringBuilder;
523                this.maxBufferSize = maxBufferSize;
524                this.metrics = metrics;
525        }
526
527        @Override
528        public void drain(LogOutput output, LogEvent event) {
529                output.write(event, stringBuilder.toString());
530        }
531
532        @Override
533        public void clear() {
534                stringBuilder.setLength(0);
535                // setLength(0) never touches capacity, so isOversized() here still
536                // reflects growth from whatever was just written - trimToSize()
537                // mutates the StringBuilder in place, no reassignment needed (works
538                // fine through the public final field above).
539                if (isOversized()) {
540                        stringBuilder.trimToSize();
541                        metrics.warnCounter(LogMetrics.BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC, 1);
542                }
543        }
544
545        @Override
546        public boolean isOversized() {
547                return maxBufferSize >= 0 && stringBuilder.capacity() > maxBufferSize;
548        }
549
550        @Override
551        public void encodeToBuffer(LogFormatter formatter, LogEvent event) {
552                formatter.format(stringBuilder, event);
553        }
554
555}
556
557/**
558 * A buffer that formats into a reused {@link StringBuilder} (like
559 * {@link StringBuilderBuffer}) but converts to bytes with
560 * {@link String#getBytes(Charset)} on the fully formatted string, instead of
561 * {@link DirectByteBufferBuffer}'s {@link java.nio.charset.CharsetEncoder}-based copy
562 * directly into a reused byte buffer. A separate class from
563 * {@link DirectByteBufferBuffer} rather than a branch inside it because the two hold
564 * fundamentally different backing storage ({@link StringBuilder} plus a scratch
565 * {@code byte[]} here, a reused {@link ByteBuffer} there) - {@link #isOversized()} only
566 * tracks {@link #stringBuilder}'s capacity, not the scratch {@code byte[]}, since the
567 * array is always sized exactly to the last event's encoded length and never retains
568 * excess capacity the way a reused buffer can.
569 *
570 * @see LogEncoder.Builder#useGetBytes(boolean)
571 */
572final class StringBuilderBufferBytes implements TextBuffer {
573
574        private static final byte[] EMPTY_BYTES = new byte[0];
575
576        final StringBuilder stringBuilder;
577
578        private final Charset charset;
579
580        private final LogOutput.ContentType contentType;
581
582        private final int maxBufferSize;
583
584        private final LogMetrics metrics;
585
586        private byte[] bytes = EMPTY_BYTES;
587
588        StringBuilderBufferBytes(StringBuilder stringBuilder, Charset charset, LogOutput.ContentType contentType,
589                        int maxBufferSize, LogMetrics metrics) {
590                super();
591                this.stringBuilder = stringBuilder;
592                this.charset = charset;
593                this.contentType = contentType;
594                this.maxBufferSize = maxBufferSize;
595                this.metrics = metrics;
596        }
597
598        @Override
599        public void drain(LogOutput output, LogEvent event) {
600                output.write(event, bytes, 0, bytes.length, contentType);
601        }
602
603        @Override
604        public void clear() {
605                stringBuilder.setLength(0);
606                bytes = EMPTY_BYTES;
607                if (isOversized()) {
608                        stringBuilder.trimToSize();
609                        metrics.warnCounter(LogMetrics.BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC, 1);
610                }
611        }
612
613        @Override
614        public boolean isOversized() {
615                return maxBufferSize >= 0 && stringBuilder.capacity() > maxBufferSize;
616        }
617
618        @Override
619        public void encodeToBuffer(LogFormatter formatter, LogEvent event) {
620                formatter.format(stringBuilder, event);
621                bytes = stringBuilder.toString().getBytes(charset);
622        }
623
624}
625
626/**
627 * A buffer that formats into a reused {@link StringBuilder} (like
628 * {@link StringBuilderBuffer}) but encodes directly into a reused {@link ByteBuffer} via
629 * a {@link CharsetEncoder}, instead of going through an intermediate {@code String} and
630 * {@code byte[]} the way {@code LogOutput.write(LogEvent, String)}'s default
631 * implementation does. This is the same technique
632 * <a href="https://logging.apache.org/log4j/2.x/manual/garbagefree.html">Log4j2's
633 * garbage-free logging</a> uses.
634 * <p>
635 * The {@link CharsetEncoder} work happens in {@link #encodeToByteBuffer()}, called by
636 * {@link #encodeToBuffer(LogFormatter, LogEvent)} - i.e. before
637 * {@link #drain(LogOutput, LogEvent) drain}, which appenders that separate formatting
638 * from writing ({@code LockThreadLocalBufferLogAppender},
639 * {@code SynchronizedThreadLocalBufferLogAppender}) call outside their lock.
640 * {@code drain} - called from inside the lock - therefore does nothing but write the
641 * already-encoded bytes, matching how Log4j2 confines the actual character-to-byte
642 * transcoding to a thread-local scratch buffer and synchronizes only the final copy into
643 * the shared destination.
644 * <p>
645 * Constructed for a specific {@link LogOutput.WriteMethod} - either
646 * {@link LogOutput.WriteMethod#BYTE_BUFFER}, in which case {@link #drain} calls
647 * {@link LogOutput#write(LogEvent, ByteBuffer, LogOutput.ContentType)} directly, or
648 * {@link LogOutput.WriteMethod#BYTES}, in which case {@link #drain} calls
649 * {@link LogOutput#write(LogEvent, byte[], int, int, LogOutput.ContentType)} using the
650 * backing array directly, rather than going through
651 * {@code LogOutput#write(LogEvent, ByteBuffer, ContentType)}'s default implementation
652 * (which would allocate a fresh {@code byte[]} copy every call for an output that does
653 * not itself implement that overload).
654 * <p>
655 * Not thread-safe. Like all {@link LogEncoder.Buffer}s it relies on the appender to
656 * guarantee no overlapping use.
657 */
658final class DirectByteBufferBuffer implements TextBuffer {
659
660        /**
661         * Default initial byte buffer capacity, matching Log4j2's own
662         * {@code log4j2.encoderByteBufferSize} default.
663         */
664        public static final int DEFAULT_INITIAL_BYTE_CAPACITY = 8192;
665
666        /**
667         * The buffer the formatter writes characters into. Sized in the constructor with
668         * {@code initialByteCapacity} (chars, not bytes, but close enough as a starting guess
669         * and cheaper than the alternative) instead of defaulting to {@link StringBuilder}'s
670         * own default capacity (16) - otherwise every fresh buffer pays for several growth
671         * reallocations on essentially every first event, the exact kind of per-event cost
672         * {@link #byteBuffer} below is already sized up front to avoid.
673         */
674        public final StringBuilder stringBuilder;
675
676        private CharBuffer charBuffer;
677
678        private final CharsetEncoder charsetEncoder;
679
680        private final LogOutput.WriteMethod writeMethod;
681
682        private final LogOutput.ContentType contentType;
683
684        private final int maxBufferSize;
685
686        private final int initialByteCapacity;
687
688        private final LogMetrics metrics;
689
690        private ByteBuffer byteBuffer;
691
692        /**
693         * Creates a buffer with the given write method, initial byte capacity, charset,
694         * content type to report to the output, and maximum combined size (see
695         * {@link #isOversized()}).
696         * @param writeMethod which {@link LogOutput#write} overload {@link #drain} should
697         * call - {@link LogOutput.WriteMethod#BYTES} or
698         * {@link LogOutput.WriteMethod#BYTE_BUFFER}.
699         * @param initialByteCapacity initial capacity of the byte buffer. It will grow
700         * (doubling, or to whatever a single event needs if larger) as needed and the grown
701         * capacity is kept for subsequent events.
702         * @param charset charset to encode with.
703         * @param contentType content type reported to {@link LogOutput#write}. Its
704         * {@link LogOutput.ContentType#charsetOrNull() charset}, if specified, should
705         * normally match {@code charset}.
706         * @param maxBufferSize a negative value disables {@link #isOversized()} entirely
707         * (always {@code false}). Since the direct buffer allocates the initial character and
708         * byte storage up front and counts both in {@link #isOversized()} regardless of how
709         * much of either store an event has actually used, a low {@code maxBufferSize} can
710         * make {@link #isOversized()} unconditionally {@code true} from the very first event
711         * - {@code maxBufferSize} should normally be set well above the combined initial
712         * retained capacity.
713         * @param metrics where to report {@link LogMetrics#BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC} each time
714         * {@link #clear()} actually shrinks the backing storage.
715         */
716        DirectByteBufferBuffer(LogOutput.WriteMethod writeMethod, int initialByteCapacity, Charset charset,
717                        LogOutput.ContentType contentType, int maxBufferSize, LogMetrics metrics) {
718                this.writeMethod = writeMethod;
719                this.stringBuilder = new StringBuilder(initialByteCapacity);
720                this.charBuffer = CharBuffer.allocate(initialByteCapacity);
721                this.byteBuffer = ByteBuffer.allocate(initialByteCapacity);
722                this.charsetEncoder = charset.newEncoder()
723                        .onMalformedInput(CodingErrorAction.REPLACE)
724                        .onUnmappableCharacter(CodingErrorAction.REPLACE);
725                this.contentType = contentType;
726                this.maxBufferSize = maxBufferSize;
727                this.initialByteCapacity = initialByteCapacity;
728                this.metrics = metrics;
729        }
730
731        /**
732         * Writes the already-encoded bytes to the output. Assumes
733         * {@link #encodeToBuffer(LogFormatter, LogEvent)} has already been called for this
734         * event - see the class doc for why that step happens there instead of here.
735         */
736        @Override
737        public void drain(LogOutput output, LogEvent event) {
738                switch (writeMethod) {
739                        case BYTE_BUFFER -> output.write(event, byteBuffer, contentType);
740                        case BYTES -> output.write(event, byteBuffer.array(), byteBuffer.arrayOffset() + byteBuffer.position(),
741                                        byteBuffer.remaining(), contentType);
742                        case STRING ->
743                                throw new IllegalStateException("DirectByteBufferBuffer does not support WriteMethod.STRING");
744                }
745        }
746
747        @Override
748        public void encodeToBuffer(LogFormatter formatter, LogEvent event) {
749                formatter.format(stringBuilder, event);
750                encodeToByteBuffer();
751        }
752
753        /**
754         * Encodes the current contents of {@link #stringBuilder} into the reused
755         * {@link ByteBuffer}, growing it first if needed. Deliberately not called from
756         * {@link #drain(LogOutput, LogEvent)} - see the class doc.
757         */
758        private void encodeToByteBuffer() {
759                int maxBytes = (int) Math.ceil(stringBuilder.length() * (double) charsetEncoder.maxBytesPerChar());
760                if (byteBuffer.capacity() < maxBytes) {
761                        byteBuffer = ByteBuffer.allocate(Math.max(maxBytes, byteBuffer.capacity() * 2));
762                }
763                byteBuffer.clear();
764                charsetEncoder.reset();
765                int length = stringBuilder.length();
766                if (charBuffer.capacity() < length) {
767                        charBuffer = CharBuffer.allocate(length);
768                }
769                stringBuilder.getChars(0, length, charBuffer.array(), charBuffer.arrayOffset());
770                charBuffer.limit(length);
771                charBuffer.position(0);
772                var result = charsetEncoder.encode(charBuffer, byteBuffer, true);
773                if (result.isError()) {
774                        try {
775                                result.throwException();
776                        }
777                        catch (CharacterCodingException e) {
778                                throw new UncheckedIOException(e);
779                        }
780                }
781                /*
782                 * maxBytes above already sized the buffer to fit the worst case so flush should
783                 * never overflow, but check defensively rather than silently truncate.
784                 */
785                var flushResult = charsetEncoder.flush(byteBuffer);
786                if (flushResult.isOverflow()) {
787                        throw new IllegalStateException("CharsetEncoder flush overflowed despite pre-sized buffer");
788                }
789                byteBuffer.flip();
790        }
791
792        @Override
793        public void clear() {
794                stringBuilder.setLength(0);
795                charBuffer.clear();
796                // Checked before byteBuffer is touched below, so this still reflects
797                // growth from whatever was just drained. stringBuilder.trimToSize()
798                // mutates in place; byteBuffer and charBuffer aren't final (they're already
799                // reassigned during growth in encodeToByteBuffer()) so reallocating them back
800                // down here needs no new field-mutability changes either.
801                if (isOversized()) {
802                        stringBuilder.trimToSize();
803                        charBuffer = CharBuffer.allocate(initialByteCapacity);
804                        byteBuffer = ByteBuffer.allocate(initialByteCapacity);
805                        metrics.warnCounter(LogMetrics.BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC, 1);
806                }
807        }
808
809        @Override
810        public boolean isOversized() {
811                return maxBufferSize >= 0
812                                && (stringBuilder.capacity() + charBuffer.capacity() + byteBuffer.capacity()) > maxBufferSize;
813        }
814
815        CharBuffer charBuffer() {
816                return this.charBuffer;
817        }
818
819}
820
821/*
822 * Not an AbstractEncoder since it needs to hand out either a StringBuilderBuffer or a
823 * DirectByteBufferBuffer depending on the output's WriteMethod hint - see buffer(hints).
824 */
825final class FormatterEncoder implements LogEncoder, LogReporter.Reportable {
826
827        private final LogFormatter formatter;
828
829        private final Charset charset;
830
831        private final ContentType contentType;
832
833        private final int maxBufferSize;
834
835        private final int initialBufferSize;
836
837        private final boolean useGetBytes;
838
839        private final LogMetrics metrics;
840
841        private final @Nullable String description;
842
843        FormatterEncoder(LogFormatter formatter, Charset charset, ContentType contentType, int maxBufferSize,
844                        int initialBufferSize, boolean useGetBytes, LogMetrics metrics, @Nullable String description) {
845                super();
846                this.formatter = formatter;
847                this.charset = charset;
848                this.contentType = contentType;
849                this.maxBufferSize = maxBufferSize;
850                this.initialBufferSize = initialBufferSize;
851                this.useGetBytes = useGetBytes;
852                this.metrics = metrics;
853                this.description = description;
854        }
855
856        @Override
857        public void report(Appendable out) throws IOException {
858                out.append("contentType=").append(contentType.contentType());
859                Charset cs = contentType.charsetOrNull();
860                if (cs != null) {
861                        out.append("; charset=").append(cs.name());
862                }
863                if (description != null) {
864                        out.append(", description=\"").append(description).append("\"");
865                }
866        }
867
868        @Override
869        public Buffer buffer(BufferHints hints) {
870                return switch (hints.writeMethod()) {
871                        case STRING -> StringBuilderBuffer.of(new StringBuilder(initialBufferSize), maxBufferSize, metrics);
872                        case BYTES,
873                                        BYTE_BUFFER ->
874                                useGetBytes
875                                                ? new StringBuilderBufferBytes(new StringBuilder(initialBufferSize), charset, contentType,
876                                                                maxBufferSize, metrics)
877                                                : new DirectByteBufferBuffer(hints.writeMethod(), initialBufferSize, charset, contentType,
878                                                                maxBufferSize, metrics);
879                };
880        }
881
882        @Override
883        public void encode(LogEvent event, Buffer buffer) {
884                switch (buffer) {
885                        case TextBuffer tb -> {
886                                tb.clear();
887                                tb.encodeToBuffer(formatter, event);
888                        }
889                        default -> throw new IllegalStateException("Unsupported buffer: " + buffer.getClass());
890                }
891        }
892
893}
